research_rationale: War-emergency delegation, signed 1946-05-23 (Truman): four items. Item 1 delegates to the Director of the Office of Defense Transportation the presidential allocation authority over transportation equipment (Act of June 28, 1940, as amended by Title III of the Second War Powers Act); item 2 subjects War Shipping Administration vessel allocations to the Director's priorities; item 3 lets the Director act through others; item 4 says nothing in the order limits Civilian Production Administration authority under EOs 9125 and 9638. EO 9919 (signed 1948-01-03, 13 FR 59 paragraph 4) added the Joint Resolution powers over transportation to the ODT delegation and said the named orders, including EO 9729, "are amended accordingly" (a later amendment, not an end). EO 10065 (signed 1949-07-06, 14 FR 3719) states that the Office of Defense Transportation and the office of its Director "is hereby terminated", effective as of July 1, 1949 (its section 4), and transfers to the Interstate Commerce Commission only the liquidation functions, including those under EOs 9462, 9554 and 9693; it does not name EO 9729, although the Federal Register disposition note reads "Revoked by: EO 10065, July 7, 1949". The abolition of the delegate on 1949-07-01 is the best-supported end of items 1 and 3, but items 2 and 4 depend on the War Shipping Administration and the Civilian Production Administration, and an earlier end for them is not excluded from held sources, so a single exact first end is not established. Force on 2026-10-14 is no.

research_rationale: EO 12701 (55 FR 5953, signed 1990-02-14) deletes the second sentence of section 1 of EO 12334 and inserts "One member shall be designated by the President as Chairman." in its place. The command is self-executing and complete on signing, so the whole order (one clause) ended on 1990-02-14 by performance on issue. The inserted text survived inside EO 12334 until EO 12863 (signed 1993-09-13) revoked EO 12334 as amended in its Sec. 3.3; EO 12863 does not name EO 12701, so it is a parent-end event and not this order's end. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register disposition notes) found no other later instrument that names EO 12701.
savings_reason: The substituted sentence took effect inside EO 12334 and continued there until EO 12863 Sec. 3.3 revoked EO 12334 as amended (signed 1993-09-13); EO 12701 kept no separate force of its own. This follows the strike-and-insert ruling: the amendment continues in the parent until the parent ends.
earlier_end_check: No earlier end exists: the command was performed on signing, 1990-02-14, and the order sets no later effective date. The only later instrument reaching it is EO 12863 (1993), which revokes the parent EO 12334 as amended and cannot be an earlier end of a command already performed in 1990.
scope_check: One clause covers the whole order: a single sentence amending section 1 of EO 12334. The held Federal Register page carries the heading (Executive Order 12701 of February 14, 1990, Amending Executive Order No. 12334), so identity is confirmed. No exception or partial scope appears.

research_rationale: EO 11294 (31 FR 10601, signed 1966-08-04) has four sections. Sec. 1 adds paragraph (o) to Section 1 of EO 10621 (per diem delegation to the Secretary of Defense for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions); Sec. 3 substitutes paragraph (9) of Section 1 of EO 11230; Sec. 4 supersedes EO 10970 to the extent not already superseded. Each is a self-executing amendment or supersession spent on signing, 1966-08-04. Sec. 2 is a continuing delegation to the Secretary of State of the President's per diem authority for areas outside the United States; it ended on 1986-07-01 when EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294, in the same order that re-delegated the successor authority to the Secretary of State (Sec. 2) and revoked paragraph (o) of EO 10621 (Sec. 1). EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 on 1971-07-22. The latest clause end, 1986-07-01, is the whole-order end. No held text shows an earlier end of Sec. 2, and the bounded searches found no other instrument naming EO 11294 as amended or revoked.
savings_reason: Paragraph (o) added by Sec. 1 continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" on 1986-07-01, and paragraph (9) substituted by Sec. 3 continued in EO 11230 until EO 11609 superseded that parent on 1971-07-22; both are consequences in the parent orders, not continuing commands of EO 11294. The Sec. 2 delegation was replaced by the delegation in EO 12561 Sec. 2 under the 1985 Act. Per diem rates fixed under the delegation are accrued results.
earlier_end_check: Sec. 1, 3 and 4 ended on issue, 1966-08-04, so nothing earlier exists. For Sec. 2, the held orders that name EO 11294 are EO 11609 (Sec. 11(5) supersedes only Section 3) and EO 12561 (Sec. 3 revokes the whole order); EO 12396 amends EO 10621 but leaves paragraph (o) and names no part of EO 11294. EO 11609 Sec. 1(2) delegates the 5 U.S.C. 5702(a) per diem authority outside the 48 contiguous states to the Office of Management and Budget; it does not name or supersede Sec. 2 and is not shown to extinguish it. The text of the 1985 Act (Pub. L. 99-234) and of 5 U.S.C. 5702 and 5707 is not held, so a statutory change before 1986-07-01 is not excluded by statute text; the end is therefore claimed from the express revocation in EO 12561 together with its successor delegation, and no held source shows an earlier lapse.
scope_check: Four clauses, matching the four sections of the held Federal Register text: Sec. 1 (amends EO 10621), Sec. 2 (delegation to the Secretary of State), Sec. 3 (amends EO 11230), Sec. 4 (supersedes EO 10970). The only partial change is EO 11609 Sec. 11(5), which reaches Sec. 3 alone. Note: the Federal Register disposition note names the superseded order as EO 10960, while the held text of Sec. 4 reads "Executive Order No. 10970"; the claim follows the held text.
independent_command_check: Sec. 2 is the only command with its own continuing force; Secs. 1, 3 and 4 act on other orders and ended on issue, with their consequences continuing inside the parent orders. Sec. 2 stands independently of Sec. 3: the supersession of Sec. 3 by EO 11609 did not touch it.
savings_check: EO 12561 contains no savings clause for acts under EO 11294 in its Sec. 1 to 3. Rates already fixed under the delegation are accrued results; paragraph (o) and paragraph (9) lived in the parent orders, as stated in the savings reason.

research_rationale: Amendment-only order, signed 1982-01-20 (Reagan): fourteen clauses (lead and sections 1 to 13) amend the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1969 (Revised edition). Under the strike-and-insert ruling each amendment is spent on issue and its text continued in the Manual until the Manual ended. EO 12473 (April 13, 1984), read in the held Federal Register text, states that the 1969 Manual "prescribed by Executive Order No. 11476, as amended by Executive Order Nos. 11835, 12018, 12198, 12233, 12306, 12340, 12383, and 12460 is hereby rescinded, effective August 1,1984". The Federal Register disposition note on this order reads "Amends: EO 11476, June 19, 1969 (which was rescinded by EO 12473, April 13, 1984)". Later amending orders EO 12383 and EO 12460 only recite EO 12340. The reading is therefore that EO 12340 was spent on issue (1982) and its consequence ended with the Manual on 1984-08-01, but EO 12473 is not citable from the packet and fourteen clause-level effective dates were not individually confirmed. Kind: amendment of a code (Manual).

research_rationale: Land transfer, signed 1958-02-22 (Eisenhower, 23 FR 1191): 16.75 acres in Kern County, California are excluded from Naval Petroleum Reserve No. 2 and transferred from the Navy to the Housing and Home Finance Agency "for defense-housing purposes", "subject to the continuation until termination of all valid existing permits, easements, rights-of-way, and other rights heretofore granted and administered by the Secretary of the Navy", with the oil, gas and other mineral rights retained in the reserve; the order modifies the order of December 13, 1912. The transfer and exclusion are self-executing and were complete on signing, but no OWN_TEXT spent-on-issue record exists because of the "until termination" proviso, and the frozen whole-order clause (characters 1446 to 13582) runs across the contents page and masthead between pages 1191 and 1193. No held later instrument names the order (the bounded name search and the three machine searches found nothing). Kind: land and property order (exclusion and transfer of a tract, reservation of minerals). The command is not a continuing duty, so force on 2026-10-14 is no as a command, with the reserved mineral rights and the preserved permits as surviving property consequences whose end is not shown by a held source.

research_rationale: EO 9155 (7 FR 3277, signed 1942-05-01) approves Civil Service Commission regulations on efficiency-rating boards of review, effective July 1, 1942. The clause inventory has eleven clauses: items 1, 2, 3(a) to 3(e), 4, 5, 6 and 7. EO 9252 (7 FR 8079, signed 1942-10-09) superseded the regulations in EO 9155 in its item 8 and made them effective immediately (the Federal Register text reads "effective immediately" with a soft hyphen in the held bytes), so items 1 to 6 ended on 1942-10-09 by express supersession. Item 7, which makes the regulations effective on July 1, 1942 and supersedes the EO 8748 regulations, was performed on that date; the EO 9252 supersession is a later event for it. The whole-order end is the latest clause end, 1942-10-09. The bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register disposition notes) show no other later instrument.
savings_reason: Rating adjustments and board decisions made under the regulations between July 1 and October 9, 1942 are accrued results. EO 9252 provides that only its own successor-service provision operates retroactively (to July 1, 1941); it contains no clause keeping EO 9155 alive after supersession.
earlier_end_check: The earliest ending found for items 1 to 6 is the express supersession by EO 9252 on 1942-10-09, effective immediately. Item 7 ended on its own stated effective date, 1942-07-01, by performance. The Federal Register disposition note names the same supersession. No held text shows an earlier end of any clause, and the bounded name search found no other order that supersedes or amends EO 9155.
scope_check: Eleven clauses matching the numbered items of the held Federal Register text. The approving sentence at the head of the order ("I hereby approve the following regulations prescribed by the Civil Service Commission") is the vehicle for the items and has the same lifecycle as the regulations it approves. EO 9252's retroactive exception relates only to the provision in its own Section 3 authorizing members of boards of review to serve until successors are appointed, not to any clause of EO 9155.
independent_command_check: Item 7 (effective date and replacement of the EO 8748 regulations) is the only command with a separate timing: it was performed on July 1, 1942, earlier than the supersession of the other items. The remaining items are rules of procedure that cannot survive the supersession of the regulations themselves.
savings_check: Neither EO 9155 nor the supersession sentence of EO 9252 contains a savings clause for rating appeals pending on October 9, 1942; EO 9252 restates the procedure, so accrued decisions are results and not continuing commands.

research_rationale: Fixed-term extension: EO 12753 (56 FR 10501, signed 1991-03-08) extends the section 126a(2) EURATOM cooperation period to March 10, 1992 and supersedes EO 12706 on its effective date. EO 12791 (signed 1992-03-09) states that EO 12753 "shall be superseded on the effective date of this Executive order" and has no delayed effective date, so the first end is 1992-03-09 (own-terms date March 10, 1992 is one day later). A trial assembly with the held EO 12791 text failed the working-text check because that text requires a page check; the claim is therefore not filed. Later extension orders EO 12840 and EO 12903 only recite EO 12753. Kind: fixed-term extension plus a one-time supersession; force on 2026-10-14 is no.
savings_reason: The extension covered a period that ended by March 10, 1992, and EO 12791 supplanted it; the order text carries no savings clause and the bounded searches found no continuing effect. Continued nuclear cooperation after 1992 rested on the successor extension orders, not on EO 12753.

savings_check: No savings clause appears in EO 12753 or in the supersession sentence of EO 12791; the bounded searches found no continuing effect.
